name: Narrow Bridge
spec: yellow diamond with black legend NARROW BRIDGE
meaning: The bridge ahead is narrower than the road.

snippets.back: Do not pass within one hundred feet before a posted narrow bridge, viaduct or tunnel.
Warning signs also flag slippery-when-wet pavement, a narrow bridge, cattle crossings and deer crossings.
Slow for heavy rush-hour traffic, narrow bridges, tunnels, and toll-booth areas that limit maneuvering space.
Slow zones calling for lower speed and extra attention include shopping centers, schools, parks and playgrounds, residential streets, rush hour, narrow bridges, toll plazas and rail crossings.
Pass one car per maneuver after scanning people, narrow bridges and road hazards that could steal the gap.
Narrow bridges and tunnels may require slower travel because opposing vehicles pass closer together.

Low Clearance bars vehicles taller than the posted height, Slippery Surface warns to drive slowly in wet weather without sudden acceleration, quick braking, or fast turns, Soft Shoulder warns not to leave the pavement except in an emergency, Narrow Bridge requires staying in your lane, and One Lane Bridge allows one vehicle at a time once clear of oncoming traffic.

You must not pass within one hundred feet of or while crossing any intersection or railroad crossing, nor within one hundred feet of a posted narrow bridge, viaduct or tunnel, and the end of a no passing zone only means visibility has improved, not that passing is safe.

result.summary: DE states narrow bridges require slower travel because opposing vehicles pass closer together, and FL states Narrow Bridge requires staying in your lane, consistent with bridge narrower than road. No snippet states yellow diamond shape, color, or legend.
